understanding: The task is to resolve 17 remaining critical data-path bugs in project 'oko' identified by an adversarial audit, prior to the first model training. The bugs are documented in AUDIT_FINDINGS_2026-06-24.md and grouped into five clusters: (A) FRAME-SYNC, (B) CROP-NAMING, (C) DATASET-EXPORT, (D) FINETUNE-GATE, and (E) MISLABEL. Three fixes have already been committed and must not be redone. Each remaining fix must be atomic, include a regression test, and pass architectural review. Clusters A-D must be fully green before any training launch. The approach must be DISCUSS-First, meaning decomposition into atoms with rationale, tradeoffs, and confidence before implementation.
summary: Decompose the 17 outstanding bugs into 14 atomic fixes (some bugs are tightly coupled and can be addressed by a single atomic change) across five clusters. Each atom includes a precise statement of the fix, the reason it is required, tradeoffs considered, and a confidence level. Regression tests are specified per atom. The plan ensures clusters A-D are completed and verified before training, with architectural review gate at each cluster. The FINETUNE-GATE cluster D is re-architected from scratch because commit 99034ac5 is confirmed non-functional. Cluster E is lower priority but still included for completeness.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster A: Fix frame selection logic to crop from the event's own frame (pending.frames[0]) instead of the last frame in the buffer.
decision_atoms.reason: Currently the system crops from the last frame (~11s after event), causing background mismatches (person/cat label on empty background). Using the event's first frame ensures the crop corresponds to the detection moment.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires ensuring pending.frames[0] is always available and not garbage-collected before cropping; may increase memory retention slightly.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster A: Add regression test that simulates a detection event, advances time, and verifies the cropped image matches the event frame, not a later frame.
decision_atoms.reason: To prevent regression of the frame-sync bug and validate the fix under simulated real-world conditions.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Test must mock or use a controlled frame buffer to be deterministic; slight overhead in test setup.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster B: Change crop naming to include camera_id and a monotonically increasing, persistent sequence number (or UUID) instead of frame_id only.
decision_atoms.reason: Using frame_id alone causes collisions when frame counters reset on restart or across different cameras, leading to overwrites and data loss.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Increases filename length and requires a sequence counter persisted across restarts; slightly more complex naming logic.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster B: Add regression test that generates crops from multiple cameras and across simulated restarts, verifying zero filename collisions.
decision_atoms.reason: Ensures the new naming scheme eliminates collisions under all identified scenarios.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Test must simulate camera IDs and counter resets; may need temporary filesystem isolation.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster C: Fix YOLO label coordinates to be relative to the crop, not the full frame, when exporting cropped images.
decision_atoms.reason: Currently bbox coordinates are computed against the full frame but the exported image is a crop, causing misaligned annotations that poison training data.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires coordinate transformation (shifting origin to crop top-left) during export; must handle edge cases where crop exceeds frame bounds.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster C: Fix missing-image handling to skip label generation entirely when the source image is missing, preventing orphan labels.
decision_atoms.reason: Orphan labels (annotation without corresponding image) break dataset integrity and cause training crashes or silent errors.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a pre-check for image existence; may slightly slow export but prevents data corruption.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster C: Fix background-class handling to never produce a positive bbox; background should be implicit (no label) or explicit negative example.
decision_atoms.reason: Current code generates a positive bounding box for 'background' class, which is semantically incorrect and degrades model performance.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires filtering logic in export; must ensure background frames are either skipped or exported with empty label files.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster C: Preserve frame width and height metadata in exported dataset manifests.
decision_atoms.reason: frame_w/h are currently lost, making it impossible to correctly normalize coordinates or reconstruct original aspect ratios downstream.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds fields to export schema; backward compatibility may require a version bump in dataset format.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster C: Add regression tests for each DATASET-EXPORT sub-bug: bbox correctness after crop, orphan label prevention, background handling, and metadata preservation.
decision_atoms.reason: Each sub-bug is distinct and requires targeted verification to ensure no regression.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Multiple test cases increase test suite size but are necessary for critical data-path coverage.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster D: Remove classification-probs computation from detection model outputs; detection models do not produce meaningful classification probabilities.
decision_atoms.reason: The current code incorrectly applies softmax over detection outputs, yielding nonsense probabilities that fail to gate bad data.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Loss of a potential (but broken) gating signal; replacement with detection confidence threshold is simpler and correct.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster D: Replace numeric class indices with human-readable class names in all gating logic and logs.
decision_atoms.reason: Using raw indices caused mismatches and made debugging impossible; names are stable across model updates and human-auditable.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires a mapping table maintained alongside model config; slight overhead but critical for correctness.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster D: Implement a lightweight orchestrator that sequences gating checks (confidence threshold, class whitelist, etc.) and halts pipeline on failure.
decision_atoms.reason: No orchestrator existed, so the broken gating was silently bypassed. An explicit orchestrator ensures gating is always executed and failures block training data ingestion.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds architectural component; must be designed to be non-blocking for valid data and fail-safe (default-deny on error).

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster D: Add integration regression test that feeds a mix of valid and invalid detection outputs through the gate and verifies correct accept/reject decisions.
decision_atoms.reason: End-to-end validation that the entire FINETUNE-GATE cluster works as intended after re-architecture.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Integration test is more complex and slower than unit tests but necessary given previous complete failure.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster E: Fix trigger_detection to require a valid track_id, not just category, before generating a training example.
decision_atoms.reason: Triggering on category alone can fire on transient false positives; requiring a tracked object ensures temporal consistency and reduces mislabels.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: May slightly reduce number of training examples (false positives are no longer captured), but improves label quality significantly.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster E: Add VLM verification step that compares class_name from the detector with a VLM query on the crop before accepting the label.
decision_atoms.reason: Detector class_name is not verified against visual content, leading to confident mislabels. VLM cross-check catches discrepancies.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds latency and cost (VLM API call) to the labeling pipeline; can be made asynchronous or sampling-based to mitigate.

decision_atoms.statement: Cluster E: Add regression tests for track_id requirement and VLM cross-verification logic.
decision_atoms.reason: Both changes alter labeling behavior and must be validated to avoid over-filtering or under-filtering.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: VLM test may need mocking to avoid external API calls in CI; track_id test is straightforward.

assumptions: The AUDIT_FINDINGS_2026-06-24.md file contains exact line numbers and descriptions for all 17 bugs, and the three already-fixed bugs are clearly marked.
The operator's commits (771b8dd, 050cb4c, a83b983) are correct and do not need rework; they do not overlap with the remaining clusters.
The codebase is in Python and uses pytest, as implied by the verify=pytest constraint.
The FINETUNE-GATE cluster D is completely non-functional despite commit 99034ac5, requiring a from-scratch reimplementation rather than patching.
A VLM service or mock is available for the MISLABEL cluster E verification step.
The 'DISCUSS-First' approach means this decomposition plan will be reviewed and discussed before any code changes are made.
Clusters A-D must be fixed and verified before training; cluster E can be addressed in parallel or subsequently but is included for completeness.
Regression tests will be integrated into the existing pytest suite for project oko.

risks.risk: The FINETUNE-GATE re-architecture introduces new bugs due to complexity and tight coupling with model output formats.
risks.mitigation: Extensive integration testing with real model outputs; architectural review by two senior engineers; gradual rollout with shadow mode before enforcing gating.

risks.risk: Crop naming changes may break downstream consumers that rely on the old naming convention.
risks.mitigation: Provide a migration script and maintain backward compatibility via symlinks or a lookup table during transition period.

risks.risk: VLM verification in cluster E adds latency and cost, potentially slowing the pipeline below acceptable thresholds.
risks.mitigation: Implement as an optional sampling check (e.g., 10% of labels) with a timeout; make configurable per environment.

risks.risk: Regression tests may not cover all edge cases, leading to undiscovered regressions in production.
risks.mitigation: Combine synthetic tests with a curated set of real-world adversarial examples from the audit; run tests in CI on every commit.

risks.risk: Architectural review bottleneck delays fixes and blocks training schedule.
risks.mitigation: Schedule review slots in advance; prepare detailed design docs per cluster to accelerate review; empower senior developers to approve minor atoms.

minimal_version: Fix clusters A, B, C, and D with atomic changes and regression tests. Cluster E is deferred to a follow-up task. All fixes are implemented as direct patches with minimal refactoring. FINETUNE-GATE is rebuilt with essential checks only (confidence threshold, class whitelist, orchestrator). Regression tests cover happy path and known audit failures. No VLM integration; MISLABEL fixes are limited to track_id requirement only.
advanced_version: All five clusters fully resolved. Cluster D includes a robust orchestrator with pluggable gating checks, detailed logging, and metrics export. Cluster E includes VLM cross-verification with adaptive sampling and caching. Crop naming uses content-hash-based deduplication. DATASET-EXPORT produces a versioned manifest with full provenance metadata. Comprehensive regression suite includes fuzz testing, edge-case simulation, and performance benchmarks. Architectural review includes a formal design document and threat model update.
